text:
maria: Heads up — reproducible issue in the browser sample: if you press Stop during a long streaming response the last chunk sometimes throws JSON.parse.

alex: rough steps?

maria: 1) open https://internal-samples.local/sse-playground 2) start a long completion (1k+ tokens) 3) click Stop ~2s into stream -> console: "SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input" on parse. Happens ~25% runs.

jin: sounds like abort cutting an in-flight SSE data frame. Our parser expects each `data:` payload to be a full JSON object per chunk.

sam: do we differentiate between user-initiated abort vs connection drop? Currently abort just calls AbortController.abort() and we suppress retries. But that still leaves the parser trying to parse whatever buffered bytes remained.

maria: quick curl repro (server-side):
```bash
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/streams" -d '{"prompt":"long loop","stream":true}'
# hit Ctrl+C while streaming, sometimes final line is truncated
```

alex: two approaches: server guarantees flush of terminal marker on complete send, or make client parser tolerant to EOF-in-middle-of-chunk and drop trailing partial payload when abort was intentional.

jin: I prefer client tolerance + better classification. If user abort -> drop partial buf silently; if network error -> surface retryable error. We need events like `stream_aborted_by_user` vs `stream_closed_network`.

sam: agree. Also add telemetry for dropped partials so we can measure. And update SDK docs to state abort semantics clearly.

maria: I prototyped a fix in sse-parser: if controller.signal.aborted then skip final JSON.parse and emit `aborted` event instead of throwing. Patch: 
```js
// sse-parser.js (concept)
if (controller.signal.aborted) {
  emit('aborted', { reason: 'client_abort' });
  return;
}
```

jin: note: Node's abort sometimes manifests as an ECONNRESET error instead of a signal, so our Node parser must detect socket EOF and map appropriately. Add unit tests simulating partial chunk then socket close.

alex: create PR with parser change + unit tests + README update + sample app integ test. Label `area:sdk-browser`. Also add small changelog entry.

jin: opened draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/502 (WIP) — includes parser tolerance + tests that simulate truncated final event and assert no thrown parse error, and an emitted `partial_dropped` metric.

sam: for the server team: can platform consider flushing a tiny terminal event like `event: stream_end\ndata: {"ended":true}\n\n` whenever possible so proxies have a clear end boundary? Might reduce partials.

alex: good idea. But proxies and TCP buffering mean it won't solve all races. Client-side handling still needed.

maria: temporary sample-app workaround: delay abort by 40ms after user click to let buffers flush. Reduced failures locally but not a fix.

jin: I'll add tests for browser+node parity, and map abort vs network reset differently. Sam, can you add a docs blurb explaining abort semantics and the `client.cancelAndRetry()` helper we plan to add?

sam: yep. Also add telemetry event `sse.partial_chunk_dropped` with tags: sdk=js, env=browser|node, abort_type=user|network.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled. No breaking changes expected.

alex: follow-ups: - PR review and merge - samples app update once SDK API stabilizes - platform flush discussion with eng-runtime

maria: thanks all — I'll follow up with sample app PR after SDK merge :rocket:
